- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The Golden Hour occurs during the first hour after sunrise and the last hour before sunset, creating flattering light for portraits.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The user should place their subject near a window or outside during the Golden Hour, with the light source at a 45-degree angle to their face.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The assistant recommends using a reflector or a piece of white cardboard to bounce light onto the subject's face to soften harsh shadows.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Overcast skies can provide beautiful, soft light ideal for portraits.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The user should pay attention to the background and use a wide aperture (like f/1.4 or f/2.8) to blur the background and isolate the subject.

- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The user should shoot in RAW to capture maximum image data and flexibility during post-processing.
